title: The Obsidian Keep
blurb: A black keep on a cliff, a storm that never ends, and a crown nobody should wear.

gate.title: The Black Gate
gate.prose: Rain hammers the black gate of the Keep. A beggar cowers in the arch, and above you the runes of the ward seethe faintly blue.

beg.title: The Beggar's Price
beg.prose: "Keep it dry, ser," the beggar says, pressing a rune-stone into your hand. "The Warden collects the crowned. Mind the crypt stairs."

court.title: The Drowned Court
court.prose: The courtyard drowns an inch deep. Doors stand open to the chapel and the crypt stairs; a wall stair climbs into the murk.

chapel.title: The Dry Chapel
chapel.prose: Inside it is dry and impossibly quiet. A guttering candle refuses to go out. Kneeling a moment steadies you more than sleep would.

crypt.title: The Crypt Stairs
crypt.prose: The crypt breathes cold. An old watch-torch still burns in its bracket, oil and stubbornness. Something below shifts in the dark and decides you are not worth it.

choices.text: Take the torch and go back up

wall.title: Above the Storm
wall.prose: From the wall walk the storm is a sea and the Keep a ship. Far below, a second gate you never passed stands open on black water.

throne.title: The Warden's Offer
throne.prose: The throne room is empty except for the crown, floating, turning slowly. The Warden's voice comes from everywhere: take it, kneel, or burn it all.

choices.text: Touch the torch to the tapestries

crown.title: The Crowned
crown.prose: The crown fits like it was poured for you. The storm stops mid-rain, every drop hanging. Below, at the gate, a figure in your cloak looks up — and you remember to be kind to them.

warden.title: Collected
warden.prose: You kneel, and the kneeling does not stop. Centuries pass like weather. Sometimes the beggars at the gate look up at the walls and shiver, and one of them is you.

pyre.title: The Burning
pyre.prose: The tapestries catch with a sound like a held breath released. The Keep burns blue and then black, and the storm, robbed of its anchor, drowns the flames — and you — with great enthusiasm.
